name: Notre-Dame Basilica (Montreal)
scope: Twin-tower Gothic Revival basilica exterior, three entry portals and main roof; exclude interior decoration and adjacent seminary.
era: surviving exterior represented by selected dated references

review.method: Inspected local original-image contact sheets; replaced unrelated images and insufficient detail views. Acceptance permits authored exterior work, not geographic activation.
review.notes: Visible exterior geometry is useful. Unseen sides require conservative reconstruction and standard viewer map controls.

candidates.filename: Basílica de Notre-Dame, Montreal, Canadá, 2017-08-12, DD 22-24 HDR.jpg
candidates.caption: Interior of the Notre-Dame Basilica, located in the historic district of Old Montreal, in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. The interior of the basilica, built in Gothic Revival style, is impressive with vivid colors, stars and filled with hundreds of intricate wooden carvings and several religious statues. It was built between 1823 and 1829 after a design of James O'Donnell and it has become one of the landmarks of the city.
